purpose: Create discipline-specific analytical views over the already validated shared Artemis II mission evidence spine.

role_source_registry.title: Artemis I Mission Control at a Glance
Meet NASA's New Artemis II Science Officers
Meet NASA's Artemis II Moon Mission Masterminds

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: NASA describes the flight director as leading the flight-control team and maintaining overall responsibility for mission conduct.
primary_questions: What changed in the integrated mission state?
Does the condition threaten crew safety or mission success?
Which disciplines need to be coordinated?
Is a decision or contingency posture required?

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: NASA describes FDO as monitoring Orion trajectory across mission phases.
primary_questions: Where is Orion relative to the planned trajectory?
Is a correction opportunity still required?
What geometric constraint is driving the event?
What is the trajectory handoff into the next dynamic phase?

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: NASA describes FAO as leading flight-plan timeline preparation and coordinating real-time changes.
primary_questions: What activity was planned next?
Did troubleshooting or geometry change the timeline?
What activities need to be re-sequenced?
Which objectives compete for crew or mission time?

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: NASA's Orion mission-control documentation assigns EECOM environmental, life-support, consumables, thermal, and emergency monitoring responsibilities.
primary_questions: Is the crew environment safe and supportable?
Is the affected system still providing required function?
What contingency capability remains available?
Is the issue resolved in flight or carried into postflight?

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: MissionLab groups public voice, telemetry-link, network-handover, DSN, expected blackout, anomaly, and reacquisition evidence into a communications discipline view.
primary_questions: Is loss of communications expected from geometry or plasma?
Is the observed loss anomalous?
What link or network transition is publicly established?
When was contact publicly reported restored?

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: Artemis II introduced a dedicated SCIENCE console responsible for integrating lunar science and geology objectives with mission execution.
primary_questions: What science opportunity exists at this mission geometry?
Was the opportunity actually observed?
What imagery, audio, annotation, or target evidence exists?
What postflight interpretation is supported?

discipline_registry.public_role_basis: NASA describes support-room experts providing real-time technical analysis and strategic guidance to front-room flight controllers. MissionLab uses ENGINEERING_SUPPORT as a cross-system technical evidence lens rather than an asserted single console call sign.
primary_questions: What evidence constrains the technical explanation?
What root cause is confirmed, hypothesized, or unavailable?
What model or test evidence supports the response?
What remains open for postflight engineering?

shared_timeline.name: Launch
shared_timeline.summary: Artemis II mission launch and start of the shared mission clock.

shared_timeline.name: Flight Day 1 toilet fault indication
shared_timeline.summary: Crew reported a blinking toilet fault light. Mission Control and crew troubleshot the condition.

shared_timeline.name: Toilet normal operations restored
shared_timeline.summary: Crew and Mission Control restored the toilet to normal operations. Public root cause remained unavailable.

shared_timeline.name: Proximity operations and manual-control demonstration
shared_timeline.summary: Crew-controlled approach and retreat were performed within the publicly reconstructed proximity operations sequence.

shared_timeline.name: Flight Day 4 wastewater vent-line issue
shared_timeline.summary: Wastewater venting ended earlier than expected. Vent heaters, Sun-pointing, contingency collection posture, and continued engineering assessment followed.

shared_timeline.name: Outbound Trajectory Correction 3
shared_timeline.summary: OTC3 executed after two earlier outbound correction opportunities were cancelled.

shared_timeline.name: Lunar sphere-of-influence entry
shared_timeline.summary: MissionLab-derived lunar sphere-of-influence entry.

shared_timeline.name: NASA-reported Earthset
shared_timeline.summary: Earthset image captured as Earth crossed the apparent lunar limb.

shared_timeline.name: Pericynthion
shared_timeline.summary: MissionLab refined closest lunar approach geometry.

shared_timeline.name: NASA-reported Earthrise
shared_timeline.summary: NASA-reported Earthrise image as Earth re-emerged beyond the lunar limb.

shared_timeline.name: Derived total solar eclipse
shared_timeline.summary: MissionLab-derived total solar eclipse interval of 54.43 minutes, consistent with NASA's nearly 54-minute public description.

shared_timeline.name: Lunar sphere-of-influence exit
shared_timeline.summary: MissionLab-derived transition out of the lunar sphere of influence.

shared_timeline.name: Return Trajectory Correction 1
shared_timeline.summary: First publicly reconstructed return trajectory correction.

shared_timeline.name: Unexpected return-link loss
shared_timeline.summary: Unexpected return-link communications interruption before RTC2 preparation.

shared_timeline.name: Return Trajectory Correction 2
shared_timeline.summary: RTC2 executed after public communications recovery and resumption of burn preparation.

shared_timeline.name: Final Return Trajectory Correction
shared_timeline.summary: Final publicly reported return correction approximately five hours before Entry Interface.

shared_timeline.name: DSN to Near Space Network handover
shared_timeline.summary: Publicly reported handover from Deep Space Network support toward Near Space Network/TDRS support.

shared_timeline.name: Crew Module / Service Module separation
shared_timeline.summary: Orion crew module separated from the service module ahead of entry.

shared_timeline.name: Entry Interface
shared_timeline.summary: Orion reached the public Entry Interface anchor.

shared_timeline.name: Planned entry plasma blackout
shared_timeline.summary: NASA reported a planned plasma communications blackout shortly after Entry Interface, expected to last about six minutes.

shared_timeline.name: Entry communications reacquisition
shared_timeline.summary: NASA publicly reported communications contact restored during the entry sequence.

shared_timeline.name: Drogue parachute deployment
shared_timeline.summary: NASA reported drogue deployment during Orion descent.

shared_timeline.name: Main parachute deployment
shared_timeline.summary: NASA reported deployment of all three main parachutes.

shared_timeline.name: Splashdown
shared_timeline.summary: Orion splashed down in the Pacific, transitioning operations from flight to crew and spacecraft recovery.
